scope: Stratified 6-skill sample across all 4 portfolio repos — Haiku counterpart to SKILL-CALIBRATION-OPUS-SAMPLE-LATEST.json
methodology: Same A/B methodology as the Sonnet and Opus runs, but each sub-agent dispatched as Haiku instead. Same 6 skills, same task briefs as the Opus run. Arm A: Haiku sub-agent solves the task cold, no SKILL.md access. Arm B: Haiku sub-agent reads the SKILL.md and follows it. Both arms produce a real artifact. Token usage from harness's per-sub-agent usage.total_tokens — input + output + cache_creation; cache_read excluded. N=1 per skill per arm.
purpose: Complete the 3-model picture for the stratified sample. Haiku is the cheapest tier — the open question is whether it executes the SKILL.md procedures reliably or fails on multi-step recipes. If Haiku tracks the Sonnet save rate, recipes are model-invariant; if it underperforms or fails, that puts a floor on which model the skill targets.

task_briefs.review: Review pull request #149 in MikkoNumminen/mikkonumminen.dev (5 files, +225/-67). Same target as the Sonnet and Opus calibrations.
task_briefs.skill-localUpdate: Plan a local refresh pass of skills-registry.json + skills-registry.pdf for d:/koodaamista/mikkonumminen.dev. Plan only.
task_briefs.copyright-scan: Scan d:/koodaamista/AudiobookMaker/src/ for accidental third-party copyright leaks. Pass/fail verdict + file:line findings.
task_briefs.readme-drift-sync: Detect drift between d:/koodaamista/mikkonumminen.dev/README.md and the repo's actual state. Markdown drift report.
task_briefs.audit: Multi-phase robustness audit of d:/koodaamista/mikkonumminen.dev/src/. Findings with severity tags + file:line citations.
task_briefs.skill-usage: Scan local Claude Code JSONLs and produce a per-skill usage summary for the last 90 days. Markdown table.

skills.name: review
skills.notes: Haiku save rate (52%) lands BETWEEN Sonnet (63%) and Opus (39%). Haiku arm B is the cheapest of the three (28K vs Sonnet's 26K vs Opus's 35K) — almost matches Sonnet. Haiku arm A is similar to Opus (58K). The recipe pattern reproduces cleanly on Haiku — the prescribed gh-CLI walk doesn't trip the smaller model. Save rate scaling: it's not monotonic in model capability. Haiku ≈ Sonnet on directed walks; Opus diverges because cold-arm is cheaper for it.

skills.name: skill-localUpdate
skills.notes: Save rate dropped from 52% (Sonnet) to 33% (Haiku) — the only sample skill where Haiku saves substantially less than Sonnet. Haiku arm B used 10 tool uses (vs Sonnet's 2, Opus's 2) — the smaller model needed more turns to execute the prescribed pipeline. The recipe still helps but less than for capable models, because Haiku spends more tokens per recipe step. This is the predicted Haiku failure mode showing up: smaller model can follow the recipe but pays per-turn overhead.

skills.name: copyright-scan
skills.notes: Haiku save rate (57%) HIGHEST of the three models — even beats Sonnet's 49%. Haiku arm A explored aggressively (61K, 26 tool uses) like Sonnet did cold; arm B followed the structured checks tightly (26K, 14 uses, also lowest arm B of the three). For investigation-collapse skills, Haiku gets the biggest recipe benefit — the smaller model would scout exhaustively cold but compresses well to a directed walk.

skills.name: readme-drift-sync
skills.notes: Tracks Opus closely (-6% vs Opus's -4%) — both Haiku and Opus break even on this skill. Only Sonnet shows the dramatic -112% cost-more. Haiku arm A found 7 drifts (47 tool uses) vs arm B's 1 drift (30 tool uses) — arm B is more conservative under SKILL.md's calibration-immunity rules, producing fewer but stricter findings. Cost-more skills are not a Sonnet-specific pathology; they reflect skill thoroughness regardless of model.

skills.name: audit
skills.notes: Save rate 23% on Haiku vs 2% on BOTH Sonnet and Opus. Haiku is the cheapest by far per arm (92K/70K vs Sonnet's 117K/114K vs Opus's 214K/209K). The audit recipe genuinely helps the smaller model focus — arm A explored 38 tool uses unstructured vs arm B's 42 with the structured walk, but arm B was tighter. This contradicts the 'audit is rigor-bound' Sonnet/Opus finding: for Haiku, the structured walk compresses the work.

skills.name: skill-usage
skills.notes: Save rate 57% on Haiku — HIGHEST of the three models, matches the Sonnet pattern (53%) and inverts Opus's -14% cost-more. Haiku arm A re-implemented a JSONL walker like Sonnet did (63K) — the smaller model lacks Opus's 'just write a Python helper' shortcut. Arm B used 4 tool uses to invoke the prescribed scan.mjs cleanly. Strong evidence that delegation-to-tool skills are most valuable for the LEAST capable model.

headline_finding: Haiku saves 37% on average across the 6-skill sample — HIGHER than Sonnet (26%) and substantially higher than Opus (13%). The recipe-vs-cold gap INVERTS by model: it shrinks going Sonnet → Opus (smarter model needs less steering), and grows going Sonnet → Haiku (smaller model benefits more from a directed walk). Five of six skills save on Haiku vs three on Opus. The one Haiku regression is skill-localUpdate (52%→33%) because Haiku used 10 tool uses to follow the pipeline vs Sonnet's 2 — per-turn overhead dominates when the recipe is short. Concrete pattern reversals from the Opus run: audit went 2%→23% on Haiku (recipe finally pays off for the rigor walk), skill-usage went -14%→57% on Haiku (delegation-to-tool wins because the smaller model can't write a from-scratch shortcut), copyright-scan went 16%→57% (the smaller model scouts exhaustively cold, compresses dramatically with the recipe). Cross-model takeaway: scaffolding/tool-selection skills earn more by targeting smaller models. If you're routing a workload to Haiku for cost, the skills that survived the Sonnet/Opus calibration as 'always saves' are even MORE valuable.
caveats: N=1 per skill per arm — same caveat as Sonnet and Opus runs.

Both audit and skill-usage arm-B Haiku ran cleanly (no procedural deviations) — unlike the Opus run where these two were the compromised measurements. Haiku results are directly comparable to Sonnet without the asterisks.
Stratified sample of 6 across 35 calibrated skills. Pattern claims are projections; full-portfolio Haiku run would resolve sample-size concerns.
